content:
I have decided to create a "Lean companion" to my real analysis textbook Analysis I, in which the definitions, theorems, and exercises of that text are translated (hopefully in a reasonably idiomatic and Mathlib-compatible fashion) into Lean code (with the exercises being statements with sorrys in their proofs). The text replicates some core Mathlib material in its own pedagogical fashion (for instance, investing some effort in developing its own version of the natural numbers Nat) but the plan is to gradually transition over to standard Mathlib definitions and API as the text progresses. Currently I have about five sections of the textbook formalized.

This project has multiple goals: primarily it is a supplement to my existing textbook, but it could also serve as a possible introduction to Lean and Mathlib (somewhat in the spirit of the Natural Number Game, for which there is significant thematic overlap), and perhaps also serve as a data set to test various autoformalization techniques.

I have set up a separate discussion thread for feedback on this project at #general > Lean companion to "Analysis I" - discussion
